stem: A 15-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department due to severe left knee pain after landing from a jump during gymnastics practice.  Examination shows swelling and tenderness just above the patella.  While lying supine with the knee extended, she is unable to lift the left leg off the table.  Imaging confirms a complete tear of the quadriceps tendon without fracture, and surgical repair is planned.  Lidocaine injection near which of the following sites is most likely to provide adequate anesthesia for the procedure?​‌​‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌​​​​​​‌​‌​‌​​​​​​​‌​‌​​​​​​‌‌​​​​‌‌​​‌​​​‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​​​‌​​​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​​​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​​​​​​‌​​‌​​‌​​‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌​
explanation:
The femoral nerve (L2–L4) innervates the quadriceps muscles, which extend the knee; the rectus femoris also assists with hip flexion.  The nerve also provides sensation to the anterior thigh and knee regions and, through its saphenous branch, the medial leg and medial border of the foot.  It emerges from the lateral border of the psoas major, travels between the psoas and iliacus muscles, and passes beneath the inguinal ligament, lateral to the femoral artery.

A femoral nerve block is performed below the inguinal ligament, with local anesthetic deposited around the nerve lateral to the femoral artery.  This blocks sensation from the anterior thigh and knee region and can provide anesthesia for quadriceps tendon repair.  It also blocks the saphenous nerve, reducing sensation along the medial leg and medial border of the foot.

(Choice A)  The biceps femoris forms the superolateral boundary of the popliteal fossa, and the common fibular nerve follows its tendon.  A popliteal sciatic nerve block can affect both the common fibular and tibial components, anesthetizing most of the leg below the knee and foot (except the saphenous nerve distribution [eg, medial aspect]).  It does not provide adequate anesthesia for quadriceps tendon repair.

(Choice C)  The ischial spine sits between the greater and lesser sciatic notches.  It is an important landmark for a pudendal nerve block, which provides perineal anesthesia during vaginal delivery and minor perineal procedures.

(Choice D)  The saphenous nerve is a sensory branch of the femoral nerve that can be blocked near the medial tibial condyle.  This distal block can reduce sensation to the medial lower leg but does not anesthetize the more proximal femoral nerve branches supplying the quadriceps.

(Choice E)  The obturator nerve passes through the obturator canal and supplies most thigh adductors and a variable area of medial thigh skin.  An obturator nerve block does not anesthetize the quadriceps and is inadequate for repair of its tendon.

Educational objective:The femoral nerve (L2–L4) innervates the quadriceps and passes beneath the inguinal ligament lateral to the femoral artery.  A femoral nerve block below this ligament anesthetizes the anterior thigh and anterior knee region and can provide anesthesia for knee procedures (eg, quadriceps tendon repair).​‌​‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌​​​​​​‌​‌​‌​​​​​​​‌​‌​​​​​​‌‌​​​​‌‌​​‌​​​‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​​​‌​​​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​​​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​​​​​​‌​​‌​​‌​​‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌​
